thesis: XTI Aerospace is a micro-cap company pivoting from legacy indoor-positioning software (formerly Inpixon) into unmanned aerial systems. **[Fact]** The company completed a reverse merger with Legacy XTI Aircraft Company in March 2025, acquired Drone Nerds (an enterprise drone distributor) through an 83.4%-owned subsidiary, and discontinued the old Inpixon business. **[Fact]** Today, substantially all revenue comes from Drone Nerds: hardware distribution, training, and repair across wholesale, direct, and retail channels. **[Fact]** Two development divisions, Autonomous Defense Systems and domestic manufacturing, have not generated revenue. **[Fact]** The TriFan 600 VTOL aircraft program is paused while management focuses on nearer-term drone economics.
why_market_wrong: The stock may still trade like a failed SPAC shell rather than a operating drone distributor with accelerating revenue. **[Inference]** Q1 2026 revenue was **$27.7 million**, up **68%** versus Q1 2025, yet the share price near **$1.59** implies a modest enterprise value once cash is netted against debt and warrant overhang. **[Inference]** GAAP net loss of **$35.3 million** in Q1 2026 includes a **$21.4 million** non-cash warrant fair-value charge, which screens out on simple earnings metrics. **[Inference]** Complexity discount applies: reverse merger history, multiple preferred series, warrant liabilities, and negative stockholders equity keep generalist investors away even as Drone Nerds scales.
